question: What is the primary distinguishing feature of skilled care compared to custodial care?

options.A: Provision exclusively within large tertiary hospital complexes
options.B: Requirement of specialized clinical knowledge and professional execution
options.C: Focus entirely on assistance with activities of daily living
options.D: Delivery solely by family caregivers trained by doctors

explanation: Skilled care specifically demands the expertise of licensed health professionals to manage complex health needs, unlike custodial care which centers on basic daily living assistance. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why is the distinction between skilled care and custodial care critical in clinical practice?

options.A: It dictates the appropriate staffing mix, resource allocation, and clinical interventions needed
options.B: It eliminates the need for any ongoing documentation or care planning
options.C: It dictates which medical insurance policies are accepted globally
options.D: It determines whether a patient requires permanent surgical intervention

explanation: Understanding care levels ensures that patients receive the right intensity of professional medical oversight rather than just basic support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is a primary objective of skilled nursing interventions?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any future medication adjustments
options.B: Preventing secondary complications and promoting optimal recovery
options.C: Permanently transferring all decision-making to the medical team
options.D: Reducing hospital length of stay to less than twenty-four hours

explanation: Skilled care aims to stabilize patients and prevent new issues like pressure ulcers or infections from developing during recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why must care objectives in skilled nursing facilities be individualized?

options.A: Patients recover at identical rates regardless of their baseline health status
options.B: Standardized routines fail to address unique physiological and psychosocial patient needs
options.C: Regulatory bodies strictly prohibit the use of standardized care pathways
options.D: Individualized plans eliminate the need for interdisciplinary team meetings

explanation: Every patient presents with a distinct medical history and response to treatment, necessitating personalized goals for effective care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which procedure is classified as a skilled nursing intervention?

options.A: Handing a pre-measured oral analgesic to an alert client
options.B: Guiding a resident on a routine morning walk in the garden
options.C: Management and dressing of complex pressure ulcers
options.D: Assisting a stable patient with morning facial hygiene

explanation: Wound management requires clinical assessment and sterile technique, placing it firmly within the scope of skilled nursing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient with a new gastrostomy tube requires which specific skilled nursing assessment?

options.A: Checking residual volumes and inspecting the peristomal skin for breakdown
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth every fifteen minutes throughout the day
options.C: Replacing the entire feeding button independently without a physician order
options.D: Restricting all oral water intake permanently to prevent aspiration

explanation: Monitoring residuals and peristomal skin integrity helps detect feeding intolerance and infection early. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h3)

question: Who typically acts as the central coordinator synthesizing inputs across the interdisciplinary skilled care team?
explanation: Registered nurses maintain continuous contact with the patient, positioning them to coordinate observations and orders from all team members. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary contribution of a physiotherapist within a skilled care facility?

options.A: Restoring mobility, improving strength, and executing gait training
options.B: Managing financial billing and insurance documentation processes
options.C: Diagnosing underlying pathological conditions and prescribing drugs
options.D: Calculating precise caloric requirements for enteral nutrition formulas

explanation: Physiotherapists specialize in physical rehabilitation, helping residents regain functional independence in movement. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a comprehensive admission assessment in skilled care?

options.A: Replacing the need for ongoing shift-to-shift verbal communication
options.B: Fulfilling a legal requirement without influencing daily nursing actions
options.C: Determining the exact date of discharge prior to clinical stabilization
options.D: Establishing a baseline of physical, cognitive, and functional status

explanation: Baseline assessments allow nurses to detect subtle clinical changes and measure the effectiveness of subsequent interventions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why must a nursing care plan remain a dynamic, continuously updated document?

options.A: Regulatory inspectors penalize facilities that keep original assessment forms
options.B: Physicians alter medication dosages every few hours during routine rounds
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards require daily rewriting of all diagnostic codes
options.D: Patient health status and clinical needs change as recovery or decline progresses

explanation: Care plans must evolve alongside the patient to ensure interventions remain relevant and effective. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is a key safety responsibility when managing complex drug regimens in skilled care?

options.A: Allowing capable residents to dispense their own medications without review
options.B: Rigorous adherence to verification protocols and monitoring for adverse interactions
options.C: Stopping all routine medications once a patient enters a long-term facility
options.D: Delegating all intravenous administration tasks to unqualified ward assistants

explanation: Polypharmacy increases vulnerability to adverse drug events, making diligent verification and monitoring essential. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: A patient receiving intravenous antibiotic therapy in a skilled care unit develops swelling and tenderness at the insertion site. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Increase the flow rate to flush any potential blockage in the cannula
options.B: Discontinue the infusion immediately and evaluate the site for infiltration
options.C: Document the observation in the chart and wait for the morning medical round
options.D: Apply a warm compress over the site and continue the prescribed infusion

explanation: Swelling and tenderness indicate possible infiltration or phlebitis, requiring immediate cessation of the infusion to prevent tissue injury. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of restorative nursing care?

options.A: Focusing solely on terminal comfort measures and pain management
options.B: Replacing professional physical therapy sessions with basic ward exercises
options.C: Providing complete physical assistance for every movement a resident attempts
options.D: Integrating rehabilitation principles into daily routine activities to maintain function

explanation: Restorative care empowers residents to retain their remaining independence by practicing skills during everyday routines. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why are regular repositioning schedules critical for immobile residents receiving skilled care?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any nutritional support or hydration
options.B: They guarantee complete recovery from chronic neurological disorders
options.C: They relieve sustained pressure on bony prominences to prevent skin breakdown
options.D: They reduce the frequency of mandatory nursing documentation entries

explanation: Relieving pressure restores blood flow to vulnerable tissue, protecting the patient against painful and dangerous pressure injuries. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why must nursing documentation in skilled care be contemporaneous?

options.A: To ensure accuracy by recording clinical events close to the time they occur
options.B: To allow administrative staff to alter vital sign records retroactively
options.C: To reduce the total number of paper forms required by the facility
options.D: To eliminate the need for verbal shift handovers between nurses

explanation: Recording care as it happens minimizes memory lapses and provides a reliable legal and clinical timeline. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)

question: How do quality assurance programs utilize clinical documentation in skilled care facilities?

options.A: To penalize individual nurses for minor typographical errors in charting
options.B: To audit care delivery, identify clinical gaps, and implement safety improvements
options.C: To advertise facility services to prospective clients and investors
options.D: To determine the personal salary increments of the medical director

explanation: Quality assurance relies on chart reviews to spot systemic trends and enhance overall patient safety and care standards. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)
